title: Three Transformer “flavours” (naming)
text:
Three Transformer “flavours” (naming)
• Encoder-only (e.g. BERT): bidirectional context inside a sentence;
blocks are often grouped as TransformerEncoder in libraries.
• Encoder–decoder (e.g. T5): encoder stack + decoder stack +
cross-attention.
• Decoder-only / causal LM (GPT, Llama, Qwen): masked
self-attention only within the sequence; generates tokens left-to-right.
LoRA + this course
Default story: decoder-only checkpoints (HF classes like
LlamaDecoderLayer, GPT2Block), not nn.TransformerEncoderLayer.

title: PyTorch / Hugging Face naming (conceptual)
text:
PyTorch / Hugging Face naming (conceptual)
• PyTorch ships nn.TransformerEncoderLayer /
TransformerDecoderLayer — generic building blocks.
• Production causal LMs usually implement custom decoder layers
(LlamaDecoderLayer, GPT2Block, . . . ) with RMSNorm, RoPE,
SwiGLU, etc.
• Under the hood, learned weights still live in standard modules
(nn.Linear, sometimes Conv1D in older GPT-2 code).

text:
Notation: hidden states at depth ℓ−1
• Omit batch dimension (same story with an extra leading axis).
• Hidden matrix Hℓ−1 ∈Rn×d: n tokens (sequence length),
d = hidden size (d model).
• Row i: contextual representation at position i before the next sublayer
(after residual/norm conventions of that architecture).

title: Self-attention:
text:
Self-attention:
three
projection
matrices
(W Q, W K, W V)
Linear maps used for queries, keys, values
Q = Hℓ−1W Q,
K = Hℓ−1W K,
V = Hℓ−1W V .
Shapes (single-head sketch): W Q, W K, W V ∈Rd×dk so Q, K, V ∈Rn×dk.
• In code these are three separate nn.Linear modules: q proj, k proj,
v proj (each stores one W 0).
• Multi-head = pack several such projections / reshape; LoRA still targets
those packed linears.

title: RoPE and ALiBi (positional machinery)
text:
RoPE and ALiBi (positional machinery)
• RoPE (Rotary Position Embedding): applies a rotation to Q, K (per
head, per position) so that QK ⊤reflects relative distances without
adding absolute position vectors (common in Llama/Mistral-class LMs).
• ALiBi (Attention with Linear Biases): adds a fixed linear bias to
attention logits that grows with |i −j| (down-weight distant keys); useful
for length extrapolation without sinusoidal embeddings (some open
models / baselines).

title: Output projection W O
text:
Output projection W O
• After heads are concatenated (multi-head), the block applies one more
linear back to width d:
Z = MHSA(Hℓ−1) = Concat(. . .) W O,
W O ∈Rdhv×d (shape varies by packing).
• In HF this is o proj / out proj: another frozen W 0 candidate for
LoRA.
• Then residual: H′ = Hℓ−1 + Z (exact layout pre-norm/post-norm
depends on model).

title: FFN: two-matrix vs SwiGLU (three-matrix)
text:
FFN: two-matrix vs SwiGLU (three-matrix)
• Classic GPT-2 style: FFN(x) = W down σ(W upx) with σ GELU/ReLU.
• Llama-style SwiGLU: uses three projections
FFN(x) = W down
�SiLU(W gatex) ⊙(W upx)

.
• Maps gate proj, up proj, down proj each hold one W 0 ∈Rdff×d or
transposed shapes depending on layout — match the model card when
counting parameters.

title: Toward LoRA (ModernLLMs.tex)
text:
Toward LoRA (ModernLLMs.tex)
• Each targeted linear map has its own frozen W 0 (pretrained weights).
• LoRA learns a low-rank ∆W = BA per targeted matrix (or merged after
training).
• Next deck / section: scaling rules (lora alpha), rank r, and QLoRA
when W 0 is quantized.
